abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a major threat to global health. It emerges in multispecies microbial communities under antibiotic exposure. This makes antibiotic spectrum --- a drug's distribution of effects across species --- a potential key parameter in resistance management. However, current theory for resistance dynamics is not well-developed for the effect of antibiotics in a multispecies setting. Analysing a well-established model in community ecology theory --- the generalized Lotka-Volterra model --- we develop a simple mathematical measure for how an antibiotic effect on one taxon (strain or species) affects another taxon through all direct and indirect interactions in a complex interaction network. Using this measure, we predict the expected effects of different antibiotic spectra on the abundance of resistant taxa in microbial communities. This furthers our understanding of the community ecology of antibiotic resistance, and provides a formal theoretical basis for empirical work on optimal antibiotic choice.
